_areas_note: Three approach systems, not one. Colfax Peak is served by Heliotrope Ridge (Glacier Creek Road) — its standard east face rises off the Grant-Colfax saddle and all three north-face ice lines are staged off the Coleman Glacier. Sherman Peak is served by Schriebers Meadow / Park Butte trailhead on Forest Road 13, by either the Easton or the Squak glacier. Hadley Peak shares nothing at all with the Black Buttes: it is a Skyline Divide / Cougar Divide peak on the north side, reached by ridge walking and second-class talus from two different logging roads, and a party heading for it never touches the Coleman. LINCOLN PEAK IS REMOVED. Both of its listed routes are approached from the Middle Fork Nooksack Road on the southwest side — the north ridge off the Thunder Glacier basin and the X Couloir out of Rankin Creek — with parties camping around 6,100 ft in the Wallace Creek and Rankin Creek basins. Going in over the Coleman is occasionally mentioned as an option and is nobody's normal choice; Lincoln belongs in a Middle Fork Nooksack / Ridley Creek zone with its own camps. Not duplicated from the Mount Baker file: Hogsback Camp, the Kulshan Cabin and Harrison sites, the 6,800 ft North Ridge glacier bivy, the 7,000 ft snow camps below the Black Buttes, the Colfax-Grant saddle bivy, Sandy Camp and the Railroad Grade and Morovitz Meadow camps. Colfax parties overwhelmingly sleep at the Hogsback and Sherman parties on the Easton side sleep at Sandy Camp, so those are the base cases and are already written; what follows is what these satellites need on top.

sites.name: Crag View, Squak Glacier
sites.capacity: The established climbers' camp on the Squak, with room for several parties on gravel benches and snow platforms at the toe of the glacier; quieter than the Easton side even on a summer weekend
sites.water: No potable water at the trailhead or anywhere on the route. Melt channels run near the moraine edge in early summer and are gone or unreliable by August, so plan on melting snow and carry the fuel for it.
sites.permit: Mt Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mount Baker Wilderness. No climbing permit and no overnight backcountry permit, but camping below 6,000 ft on this route is prohibited, which is the practical reason Crag View exists where it does. A recreation pass is required to park at the Park Butte trailhead. Party size is capped at 12 once you enter the wilderness, campfires are prohibited, and there is no toilet anywhere on the route — carry blue bags, which are handed out free at the ranger offices in Sedro-Woolley and at Glacier. Nothing may be buried in snow or dropped into a crevasse or moat.
sites.notes: This is the camp for Sherman Peak's Squak Glacier route and it is the site the Mount Baker file does not cover, since everything written there is on the Easton or the Coleman. It sits about 3.5 miles and 3,300 ft above Schriebers Meadow: the Park Butte trail past Sulphur Creek and the meadows, then a climbers' path leaving the trail around 4,600 ft and running up onto the moraine. From here the route makes a rising traverse of the Squak toward Sherman's south ridge, roughly 3,600 ft to the summit. The Squak is an early-season objective and the reason is specific — a bergschrund opens across the line as the season goes on and can shut the route down entirely by late summer, so a July plan is a different proposition from a May one. The lower part of the approach is outside the wilderness and carries snowmobile traffic into early July. Forest Road 13 off Road 12 is gravel and holds snow late; check it before a long drive.

sites.name: Upper Squak benches, Sulphur moraine and the rock prow
sites.capacity: Dug snow platforms and moraine gravel for one or two parties along the right-hand edge of the glacier, with a second bench under a rock prow several hundred feet higher; no established sites and no shelter
sites.water: None. Melt snow. Anything running here in early summer is a bonus and will not be there later in the year.
sites.permit: Mount Baker Wilderness rules as at Crag View — no permit to camp, recreation pass at the Park Butte trailhead, 12-person party limit, no campfires, all waste packed out in blue bags.
sites.notes: Parties who want Sherman's summit day short move above Crag View and camp on the Sulphur moraine at the glacier's edge around 7,000 ft, or push on to the flatter ground below the rock prow closer to 7,600 ft. The gain is real, since it takes a good chunk out of the traverse to the south ridge and puts you at the base of the steep snow with the night's freeze still holding. The cost is a fully exposed camp on a volcano's south flank, where wind is the usual reason parties come back down to Crag View, and you are already on glacier and roped to get here. Camping this high also means committing to melt water, which drives fuel weight up. Where exactly the platforms are usable moves year to year with the crevasse pattern, so arrive with daylight to scout rather than in the dark.

sites.name: Coleman Glacier bivy under the Black Buttes north faces
sites.capacity: Dug platforms for a party or two on the flats out from the foot of the faces; no established site and nothing to shelter behind
sites.water: None to rely on. Melt snow. Surface runoff sometimes appears on the rock of the buttes in a hot spell and should not be planned around.
sites.permit: Mt Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mount Baker Wilderness. No climbing permit and no overnight permit; camping is dispersed. Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass to park at Heliotrope Ridge. Party limit 12, no campfires, no toilets on the route, waste packed out in blue bags available free from the ranger offices. Registering a climb is voluntary and worth doing.
sites.notes: Colfax's three north-side ice lines — the Cosley-Houston, the Polish Route and Kimchi Suicide Volcano — all start off the Coleman somewhere near 8,000 ft, and this is the staging ground for a party that does not want to cover the whole approach from the Hogsback on climb morning. The important thing about it is where you do not put the tent: ice and rock come off the Colfax seracs onto this part of the glacier with some regularity, so the usable camping is out on the flats well clear of the fall line, never tucked in against the toe of the face because it looks sheltered. Many parties skip this camp entirely and climb these routes in a long day from the trailhead or from the Hogsback, which is a reasonable answer to the same hazard. These are cold-season routes, roughly late October into May, and the ice changes character completely across that window. Access is the current constraint rather than the camp: Glacier Creek Road washed out in the December 2025 floods and has been closed to vehicles well below the trailhead, open to walkers and bikes at the contractors' discretion with repairs anticipated through 2026 — confirm the road before planning to carry a heavy load.

sites.name: Cougar Divide meadow camps
sites.capacity: A handful of small sites in the meadows near the head of the divide; pick rocky ground rather than heather, which recovers slowly here
sites.water: Better than anywhere else on this side. A creek fed by a lingering snowfield runs at the upper camp through most of the season, and there are ponds along the divide that are worth treating and not drinking untreated. Water gets scarce once the snowfield goes.
sites.permit: Mt Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mount Baker Wilderness. No overnight permit and no climbing permit. The access road is gated seasonally, closed from the start of November until the second week of July for wildlife, which is the single biggest planning constraint on this side of the mountain. Party size 12, no campfires, pack out all waste.
sites.notes: This is the north-side approach to Hadley Peak and it has nothing to do with the Black Buttes or the Coleman — a party here is on the far side of the mountain from the Heliotrope Ridge climbers. Cougar Divide is an unofficial, unmaintained path along the ridge crest, reached from Wells Creek Road, whose first several miles are badly potholed to the Nooksack bridge and then improve. From the meadows at the head of the divide the ground opens onto Chowder Ridge, and the connection east along the ridge leads to Hadley. The gate opening in July combined with mosquitoes that are genuinely bad here until midsummer pushes the sensible window to mid-August through early October, which is also when the talus is clear and the route is straightforward walking with the odd second-class step.

sites.name: Skyline Divide crest camps
sites.capacity: Several exposed sites along the open crest of the divide once the trail tops out; popular and visible, with no screening from wind or weather
sites.water: None at the trailhead and none along the trail after early summer, when the snow patches below the crest are gone. Carry everything or plan the trip around a lingering snowfield you have confirmed is still there.
sites.permit: Mt Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mount Baker Wilderness. A recreation pass is required at the trailhead. No campfires anywhere, party size capped at 12, all waste packed out. There is no permit or quota for camping, but the meadows are heavily used and heavily damaged, so camp on bare ground.
sites.notes: The other approach to Hadley Peak, from the west along the divide and over Chowder Ridge. The road in has been the problem for years rather than the trail: flood damage at around mile three has left the trailhead inaccessible to vehicles for extended periods with no firm repair date, and the trail has been listed as closed on that account, so this is the first thing to confirm and not an afterthought. When it goes, the crest is easy walking with big views and the last three quarters of a mile up to Chowder Ridge is talus with one steeper step before you top out west of the Hadley Glacier. Camping on the open crest means taking whatever weather arrives off the mountain, and the exposure is the reason parties often drop into the basin instead.

sites.name: Deadhorse Creek basin, below Chowder Ridge
sites.capacity: Scattered informal sites in the basin between the two divides; sheltered, low use, no facilities of any kind
sites.water: The most reliable water on the Hadley approach — the creek runs from snowmelt above the basin and holds up later than anything on the ridge crests. Treat it. This is the reason to camp here rather than higher.
sites.permit: Mount Baker Wilderness, no overnight permit required. Recreation pass at whichever trailhead you start from. Party size 12, campfires prohibited, human waste and everything else packed out — there are no toilets on either divide.
sites.notes: The basin sits between Skyline Divide and Cougar Divide, just short of the climb onto Chowder Ridge, and it solves the problem both crest camps have: it has water and it has shelter. A party approaching Hadley from either road can drop into it, sleep out of the wind, and take the ridge in the morning with full bottles. Summit day from here is short by any standard on this mountain. It is subalpine meadow and creek terrain, so camp on durable ground well back from the water. Season is the same as everything else on the north side, mid-August into early October, held back at the front end by mosquitoes and by the road gate on the Cougar Divide side and at the back end by the first real snow.
